messages:
sara: Heads-up — AcmeCorp reported SSO failures after yesterday's IdP cert rotation. They see 403s on the ACS endpoint and the app logs show 'invalid recipient'. I pulled the metadata URL and it looks truncated when our poller fetched it :confused:

ben: Got the link? can we repro in staging first or is prod-only?

sara: idp metadata: https://acme-idp.example.com/metadata (customer shared). Our metadata-poller logs show a successful 200 but body length is ~1.2k which is smaller than expected. When I curl it from my laptop I get a full XML 8k file.

kyle: interesting. can you paste the poller fetch log line?

sara: paste from poller:
```
2026-03-16T11:02:13Z metadata-poller INFO fetch https://acme-idp.example.com/metadata status=200 length=1268 etag="W/\"75-abc...\""
2026-03-16T11:02:13Z metadata-poller WARN parse failed: unexpected EOF (line 1 column 1234)
```
ingrid: that looks like the body was truncated. Could be a middlebox or CDN serving a partial response to our poller IPs. Customer's direct curl succeeding suggests some path difference. any proxies in front of poller?

ben: poller runs from our staging fleet in us-west-2. We route through internal egress NAT + our outbound proxy that applies gzip and http2. If the IdP origin mis-handles `Accept-Encoding` or http2 it could close early. I can try fetching from a staging VM without the proxy.

oncall-bot: Incident created: #INC-20260316-SSO-ACMECORP (priority=high) — auto-alerts to @ben @kyle @sara

kyle: I ran `curl -v` from a staging box (no proxy):
```
$ curl -v https://acme-idp.example.com/metadata -o metadata.xml
*   Trying 203.0.113.22:443...\n* Connected to acme-idp.example.com (203.0.113.22) port 443 (#0)\n> GET /metadata HTTP/1.1\n> Host: acme-idp.example.com\n> Accept: */*\n>\n< HTTP/1.1 200 OK\n< content-length: 8192\n< content-encoding: gzip\n<\n# file is 8k when inflated
```

kyle: but when the poller (with proxy) fetched it we recorded `length=1268`. That matches the size of a truncated gzip stream header — suggests our proxy is not passing full body or is double-decompressing and truncating.

ingrid: possible repro: proxy sets `Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate` and then decompresses, but if the downstream sends `Content-Encoding: gzip` and closes early our decompressor may see EOF and return partial bytes. We should check proxy logs for upstream `connection: close` and any 502/5xx.

ben: I checked proxy logs for that timestamp — upstream returned 200 and then `upstream_bytes_sent=1268` and `upstream_connection: close`. There's also an `upstream_ratelimit` warning in the proxy.

sara: customer sees 403s because our SAML parser fails on truncated XML, so the assertion recipient doesn't match. They rotated certs at 10:00 UTC yesterday. The metadata probably included new KeyDescriptor nodes — missing in our poller copy.

kyle: immediate workaround: ask customer to upload their IdP metadata via the support UI (we can accept manual metadata). That avoids poller and will restore login. Can you ask them to attach the full metadata XML and the rotation timestamp?

sara: pinged customer for upload and rotation time. also filed internal change to let support upload manual metadata to tenant config.

ingrid: longer-term fix: we must ensure the metadata-poller respects raw bytes and does not attempt to double-decompress. I'll open a ticket for infra to audit proxy decompression path + our http client library. Recommend instrumenting body-length vs content-length alerts.

ben: quick triage steps I ran: 1) `openssl s_client -connect acme-idp.example.com:443 -servername acme-idp.example.com` (handshake ok) 2) `curl --compressed` from proxy host to replicate headers 3) fetch via our poller container image locally -> reproduced truncated body. So it's definitely proxy-path.

kyle: proposed immediate actions:
- Support: ask customer to upload metadata XML and confirm users can login after manual upload (Sara)
- Infra: rollback proxy decompression change on staging and prod for metadata route or bypass proxy for poller (Ben/Kyle)
- SRE/Sec: verify no partial certs were installed by the IdP (Ingrid)

sara: customer uploaded full metadata.xml and confirmed they can login after I manually updated their tenant metadata in the console. Customer happy for now, asked for RCA.

ben: infra task created: INF-20260316-PIPE-230 — revert `proxy: auto-decompress` flag for metadata endpoints and add a retry-if-truncated in poller. I'll start a PR and run canary in staging.

ingrid: security note: when metadata is truncated our parser could mis-interpret nodes; add additional validation: require top-level `<EntityDescriptor>` and compute SHA256 of uploaded metadata and compare to fetched to detect partial fetches before applying.

kyle: logging action: add `fetched_length` and `content_length_header` to poller metrics and alert if mismatch > 10%.

sara: closing loop with customer: emailed RCA draft and timeline. will update ticket once infra PR is merged to prod.

ben: thanks everyone. follow-up: assign to oncall for next 48h to watch poller error rate for other customers.

oncall-bot: Assigned to @ben (oncall) until 2026-03-18T11:02:13Z

sara: TL;DR: cause = proxy decompression + upstream close causing truncated metadata; workaround = manual metadata upload; fix = revert decompression for metadata route + add poller safeties.
